Commentary of al-Qasimi (Mahasin al-Ta'wil) on surah 19, verses 1–3:

(p-4124) In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

Surah Maryam

It is named after it because it includes its extraordinary account (naba'uha al-khariq). Al-Mahayimi said: Because its story indicates that whoever withdraws from his people to worship Allah, and seeks through that the illumination of His light, it is hoped that He will unveil to him the attributes of the Truth and the world of the malakut (the unseen dominion), and wondrous marvels (karamat) will appear to him. This is among the greatest aims of the Qur'an. It was revealed in Mecca. Some scholars excluded from it the verse of prostration and the verse "And there is none of you but will pass through it" (Maryam: 71).

Muhammad ibn Ishaq narrated in the Sirah, from the hadith of Umm Salamah, and Ahmad ibn Hanbal narrated from Ibn Mas'ud, in the account of the migration to the land of Abyssinia from Mecca, that Ja'far ibn Abi Talib, may Allah be pleased with him, recited the opening of this surah to the Negus and his companions. Its verses number ninety-eight.

(p-4125) Discussion on the interpretation of His, the Exalted, words:

[1] ﴿Kaf, Ha, Ya, 'Ayn, Sad.﴾ [2] ﴿A mention of the mercy of your Lord to His servant Zakariya.﴾ (Maryam: 2) [3] ﴿When he called to his Lord with a secret call.﴾ (Maryam: 3).

﴿Kaf, Ha, Ya, 'Ayn, Sad.﴾ The discussion of these initial letters has already passed at the beginning of Surah al-Baqarah. The most correct opinion is that they are names of the surah that begins with them. It may also be that they are the predicate of an omitted subject, i.e., "this is": ﴿Kaf, Ha, Ya, 'Ayn, Sad﴾, meaning "named with it." His words, ﴿A mention of the mercy of your Lord to His servant Zakariya﴾ (Maryam: 2), are a subject whose predicate is omitted, i.e., "in what is recited to you." Or it is a predicate of an omitted subject, i.e., "what is recited is the mention of it, and Zakariya is the father of Yahya, peace be upon them both." "His servant" is either a substitute (badal) or an explanatory appositive (ʿatf bayan) for it. Al-Mahayimi said: That is, Allah's mention to us of what He showed mercy to Zakariya, peace be upon him, in accordance with the perfection of His lordship. He gave him a son perfect in the matter of prophethood. He gave him the good news Himself at one time and through His angels at another. He Himself undertook his naming and did not share it with anyone before him. Its mention to us is a great gift to us, in defining the station of prophethood, and the power of Allah and His care for His chosen one.

﴿When he called to his Lord with a secret call﴾ (Maryam: 3) is a temporal clause (zarf) modifying (rahmah), or a substitute of inclusion (badal ishtimal) from (Zakariya). Al-Nida' originally means raising the voice and making it manifest. Here it means supplication (du'a'). He observed the etiquette of supplication, which is to make it secret, because that is further from ostentation and closer to sincerity. Then he explained the supplication with his words:

(p-4126) On the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

[4] ﴿He said: "My Lord, indeed my bones have weakened and my head has glistened with grey hair, and I have never been unsuccessful in my supplication to You, my Lord."﴾

﴿He said: "My Lord, indeed my bones have weakened"﴾, meaning: they have become frail. Al-Zamakhshari said: He mentioned the bones because they are the pillar of the body, by which it stands, and they are the foundation of its structure. When they weaken, the rest collapses and its strength falls away. Also, they are the hardest and most solid part of it, so if they weaken, what is beyond them is weaker still. He used the singular, because the singular noun ("bone") denotes the category, which indicates that the weakness encompasses every individual member of it. It has also been read as "wahina" with the ha vowelled with a kasra and with a damma. ﴿and my head has glistened with grey hair﴾. Al-Zamakhshari said: He likened the whiteness of grey hair, its brightness and luminosity, its spreading through the hair, its pervading it, and its taking hold of it in every way, to the flames of fire, and he then expressed this in the form of a metaphor (isti'arah, the transfer of a word from its literal to a figurative sense). He then attributed the "kindling" (ishtial) to the place where the hair grows and springs forth, which is the head. He introduced the grey hair as a specifying noun (tamyiz) and did not add the head to a possessive, being content with the listener's knowledge that it was the head of Zakariyya. Hence this sentence is eloquent and is testified to be eloquent. Its apparent sense is that it contains two metaphors built upon two similes. The first is an explicit subordinate metaphor (tasrihiyyah tab'iyyah) in the word "ishtala" (kindled), by likening the spreading of the whiteness through the blackness to the kindling of fire, as Ibn Duraid said in his Maqsurah:

"If you see my head, its colour has resembled the dawn's streak beneath the skirts of the darkness.

The whiteness spread through its blackness ∗∗∗ like the kindling of fire in the dry wood of the ghada tree."

The second is an implicit metaphor (makniyyah), by likening the grey hair, in its whiteness and brightness, to a flame. This is based on the view that the implicit metaphor may be separated from the imaginative (takhyiliyyah) element, which is the view of the verifying scholars of the science of meanings (ma'ani). It has been said that the metaphor here is an allegorical composite metaphor (tamthiliyyah): the state of the grey hair is likened to the state of fire, in its whiteness and its spreading.

﴿and I have never been unsuccessful in my supplication to You, my Lord﴾, meaning: I have never been disappointed in my supplication to You, at a time when I was never accustomed from You except to being answered in supplication, and You never once turned me away. This is a means (tawassul) by which he seeks nearness to God, exalted is He, through the answering that had previously taken place between him and Him, following the preparation of what calls for mercy and draws compassion, namely old age and the weakness of his condition. For when He, exalted is He, has accustomed His servant to being answered over a long period, He will hardly ever disappoint him, especially when he is in dire need and in extreme poverty.

Note:

From these verses are derived the etiquettes of supplication and what is recommended in it. Among them is supplicating in a low voice, from His saying "in a low voice" (khafiyyan). Among them is the recommendation of humility in supplication and displaying lowliness, humbleness and weakness, from His saying: ﴿and my head has glistened with grey hair﴾. Among them is seeking nearness to God, exalted is He, through His blessings and His beautiful customary favours, from His saying: ﴿and I have never been﴾, etc., as we have previously mentioned.

Commentary of al-Qasimi (Mahasin al-Ta'wil) on surah 19, verses 5–6:

The discussion of the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

[5] ﴿And indeed I fear the successors after me, and my wife is barren, so grant me from Yourself an heir,﴾ [6] ﴿who will inherit me and inherit from the family of Ya'qub; and make him, my Lord, pleasing.﴾ [Maryam: 5–6].

﴿And indeed I fear the successors after me﴾ means: those who will take charge of the affairs of my kinsfolk after my death, since none of them is fit to succeed me in carrying out what I used to do: giving guidance and admonishing the servants, preserving the etiquette of the religion, and holding fast to its firm path. ﴿And my wife is barren﴾ means: she has not borne children since her youth. ﴿So grant me from Yourself an heir, who will inherit me and inherit from the family of Ya'qub﴾ [Maryam: 6] means: grant me a child who will take up the affairs that I used to be responsible for, as an heir to me and to the family of Ya'qub, in knowledge and prophethood. The words ﴿from Yourself﴾ indicate that this is by pure bounty and a breach of customary practice, since his wife was not fit for conception. They also exalt the request by attributing it to God, exalted is He, and to what proceeds from His presence. ("The family of Ya'qub") refers to his descendants, the prophets, peace be upon them. ﴿And make him, my Lord, pleasing﴾ [Maryam: 6] means: pleasing to You in word and deed.

Then Allah, exalted is He, explained the answering of Zakariyya's supplication with His saying:

Discussion on the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

[7] ﴿O Zakariyya, indeed We give you good news of a boy whose name is Yahya; We have not made for him any namesake before.﴾

﴿O Zakariyya, indeed We give you good news of a boy whose name is Yahya; We have not made for him any namesake before.﴾ That is: no equal or likeness. And it is related from Ibn ʿAbbas: no barren woman had borne someone like him before. It is also narrated that he never disobeyed, nor did he ever intend a sin.

The discussion of His saying, Exalted is He:

[8] ﴿He said, "My Lord, how will I have a boy when my wife has been barren and I have reached extreme old age?"﴾

﴿He said, "My Lord, how will I have a boy when my wife has been barren and I have reached extreme old age?"﴾ That is: a state for which there is no way of correcting it or treating it. It has been said: [it means] to train him (riyada), which is the state indicated by the words of the poet:

"And of hardship is the training of the aged (riyadat al-haram)."

Said al-Raghib (al-Raghib al-Isfahani).

Commentary on the interpretation of His words, exalted is He:

[9] ﴿He said: "So it is. Your Lord says: 'It is easy for Me, and I created you before, when you were nothing.'"﴾

﴿He said: "So it is. Your Lord says: 'It is easy for Me, and I created you before, when you were nothing.'"﴾ That is: from a human being, a drop (nutfah), a clinging clot (alaqah), and elements (anasir), and then you came into existence.

Al-Zamakhshari said: If you ask: why did he [Zakariyya] first request [a child] while he and his wife were in the state of extreme old age (al-itiyy) and barrenness (al-uqr), and then, when his request was granted, he expressed astonishment and found it unlikely? I say: so that he would be answered with what he was answered with, and the believers would grow in certainty, and the deniers would be restrained. Otherwise, Zakariyya's belief, both at the beginning and at the end, followed one path: that Allah is free of need for means (al-asbab). End of quote.

(p-4129) Abu al-Su'ud said: He, peace be upon him, said this, despite having previously prayed for it and having strong certainty in Allah's power, especially after witnessing the signs mentioned in Surah Al 'Imran, in order to magnify Allah's power and to marvel at it, and to acknowledge His favor upon him in this matter by showing that it was purely from Allah's subtle kindness (lutf) and grace (fadl), even though it was in itself among the things customarily deemed impossible, not as a way of finding it unlikely. It was also said: this was from him a question about how the child would come about, i.e., "Will there be a child while we are in this state?" So it was said to him: "So it is," i.e., "There will be a child while you two are in this state."

The discussion of His saying, may He be exalted:

[10] ﴿He said: "My Lord, appoint for me a sign." He said: "Your sign is that you will not speak to the people for three nights, though you are sound."﴾

﴿He said: "My Lord, appoint for me a sign"﴾ That is, a sign that will show me the certainty of what was foretold and the occurrence of the pregnancy, so that my heart may be at rest. ﴿He said: "Your sign is that you will not speak to the people for three nights, though you are sound"﴾ That is, you will not be able to speak to them while you are sound, without any illness in your body or in your tongue.

A subtle point:

He mentioned the nights here, and the days in Al ʿImran, to indicate that the prohibition from speaking to people continued for him, and that he devoted himself to remembrance (dhikr) and thanksgiving (shukr) for three days with their nights.

The Arabs sometimes use a figure of speech, or mention one of the two in place of the other. The point in mentioning "the nights" here and "the days" elsewhere is that this surah is Meccan and was revealed earlier, while that one is Medinan. For the Arabs, the nights precede the days, because their months and years are lunar, known by the crescents. Therefore they reckoned by them in dating, as the grammarians mentioned, so the earlier was given to the earlier.

Discourse on the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

[11] ﴿So he came out to his people from the prayer niche, and he signaled to them, saying: Glorify (Him) morning and evening.﴾

﴿So he came out to his people from the prayer niche﴾, i.e., his place of prayer or his upper chamber. ﴿And he signaled to them﴾, i.e., he gestured to them by sign. ﴿Glorify (Him) morning and evening﴾, i.e., pray to God at the two ends of the day.

Commentary of al-Qasimi (Mahasin al-Ta'wil) on surah 19, verse 12:

And His saying, exalted is He:

The discussion of the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

[12] ﴿O Yahya, take the Book with determination. And We gave him judgment while yet a boy.﴾

﴿O Yahya﴾ is a resumptive statement (isti'naf), many sentences having been omitted from it in haste to report the fulfilment of the noble promise. That promise was the existence of this boy who was given glad tidings of, and his being taught the Torah, which they used to study among themselves and by which the prophets who submitted (aslamu) to those who were Jews (alladhina hadu), and the rabbis (rabbaniyyun) and the rabbis of learning (ahbar), would judge. At that time his age was small. Therefore He mentioned him, and what He had bestowed upon him and upon his parents. That is: We said, "O Yahya: ﴿take the Book with determination﴾," that is, learn the Torah and knowledge with earnestness, eagerness and diligence. ﴿And We gave him judgment while yet a boy﴾, that is, wisdom, understanding of the Torah, knowledge, and striving in goodness, and he was a boy.

His saying, exalted is He:

﴿And compassion from Us﴾, i.e., We bestowed upon him ḥanān (compassion), which is tahannun (tenderness), ta'aṭṭuf (affection), and shafaqah (compassionate concern). [15] ﴿And peace be upon him the day he was born, and the day he dies, and the day he is raised up alive.﴾

﴿And peace be upon him﴾, that is, from Allah. ﴿The day he was born, and the day he dies, and the day he is raised up alive﴾, that is, so that he may receive everlasting bliss. Commentary on the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

[16] ﴿And mention in the Book Mary, when she withdrew from her family to an eastern place.﴾

﴿And mention in the Book﴾, i.e., the Qur'an. ﴿Mary﴾, i.e., her story. ﴿When she withdrew﴾, i.e., she isolated herself and secluded herself. ﴿From her family to an eastern place﴾, i.e., to the east of Bayt al-Maqdis (the Holy House, Jerusalem), so that they would not distract her from worship.

The discussion of the words of His, the Exalted: [17] "So she took a screen apart from them, and We sent to her Our Spirit, and it took for her the likeness of a well-proportioned man."

"So she took a screen apart from them" means: so that the sight of creation would not veil her from the lights of the Truth. "We sent to her Our Spirit" means: Jibril, who is ascribed to the station of Our greatness, for the sake of his perfection, to breathe into her. "And it took for her the likeness" means: it presented itself to her sight. "A well-proportioned man" means: of well-formed creation, complete in form.

Commentary of al-Qasimi (Mahasin al-Ta'wil) on surah 19, verse 18:

The discussion of the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

[18] ﴿She said, "Indeed, I seek refuge in the Most Merciful from you, if you should be fearing of Allah."﴾

﴿She said, "Indeed, I seek refuge in the Most Merciful from you"﴾ meaning: I seek protection in Him from you. She feared him only because she was alone in her seclusion, and she thought that he intended to have her against her will. In this is piety and chastity to a degree beyond which there is no further limit. ﴿If you should be fearing Allah﴾ meaning: if you fear Allah, the Exalted, and are mindful of seeking refuge in Him. The answer to the conditional is omitted, relying confidently on the context pointing to it; that is: then I am seeking refuge in Him; or: then do not approach me. She reminded him of Allah, the Exalted, only because what is prescribed in repelling [an evil] is to begin with the easiest and then the next easiest. So she first made him fear Allah, mighty and majestic.

The Interpretation of His Words, the Exalted:

[19] ﴿He said, "I am only a messenger of your Lord, to give you a pure son."﴾

﴿He said, "I am only a messenger"﴾ meaning: Do not fear, and do not anticipate what you imagined. For I am a messenger of your Lord, whom you sought refuge in (p-4132), who has sent me to you: ﴿to give you a pure son﴾, meaning: to be the means of his gift. And (al-Zakiyy): the one pure of sins, or the one who grows in goodness.

The Interpretation of His Words, Exalted is He:

[20] ﴿She said, "How can I have a boy when no man has touched me and I have not been unchaste?"﴾

﴿She said, "How can I have a boy when no man has touched me and I have not been unchaste?"﴾ That is: she was astonished at this and said: how can I have a boy, that is, in what manner would he come into being from me, when I am not a woman with a husband, and when unchastity is not conceivable from me?

Al-Zamakhshari said: He made the "touch" (al-mass) a metaphor for lawful marriage (al-nikah al-halal), since it is a euphemism for it, as in His words, Exalted is He: ﴿before you have touched them﴾ [al-Ahzab: 49] and ﴿or you have touched women﴾ [al-Ma'idah: 6]. Fornication is not like this; rather, it is said of it: "he committed fornication with her" (fajara biha), "he defiled himself with her" (khabutha biha), and what is similar to that. And it is not fitting that euphemisms and courtesies be observed in it. He only restricted himself in Surat Al 'Imran to His words, "no man has touched me," because this surah was revealed earlier, so it is the place of detail, unlike that one. And al-baghiy (the unchaste woman) is the woman who solicits men (al-fajirah allati tabghi al-rijal). Its form is fu'ul (fu'ul), and therefore the feminine ta' does not attach to it, because it applies equally to the masculine and the feminine, even though it has the meaning of the active participle (fa'il), as in sabur. Or it is fa'il in the sense of fa'il, and the ta' did not attach to it because it denotes intensity (al-mubalaghah).

The commentary on His saying (Exalted is He):

[21] ﴿He said: "So it will be. Your Lord says: 'It is easy for Me, and We will make him a sign for mankind and a mercy from Us, and it is a matter decreed.'"﴾

He said, meaning the angel: ﴿"So it will be. Your Lord says: 'It is easy for Me, and We will make him a sign for mankind,'"﴾ meaning (p-4133) a proof by which they may infer the perfection of the power of their Creator and Originator, who diversified their creation. He created their father Adam without a male or a female. He created Eve from a male without a female. He created the rest of the offspring from a male and a female, except for Jesus, for He brought him into being from a female without a male. Thus the fourfold division was completed, indicating the perfection of His power and the greatness of His dominion. ﴿"And a mercy from Us"﴾ meaning: for you, through this honour, and for your people, through guidance and the call to worship and to affirm the oneness of God, so that they may be guided by His guidance and seek right direction through His direction.

His saying ﴿"and it is a matter decreed"﴾ is part of Gabriel's speech to Mary. He informs her that this is a matter predetermined in the knowledge, decree and will of God, Exalted is He. Alternatively, it is part of God's report, Exalted is He, to His Prophet, may the prayers of God be upon him, and that by it He alluded to the breathing into her private part, as He, Exalted is He, said: ﴿"And Mary, daughter of 'Imran, who guarded her chastity, so We breathed into her of Our Spirit"﴾ [at-Tahrim: 12], and He said: ﴿"And she who guarded her chastity, so We breathed into her of Our Spirit"﴾ [al-Anbiya: 91].

Commentary of al-Qasimi (Mahasin al-Ta'wil) on surah 19, verse 22:

The discussion of His saying, exalted is He:

[22] ﴿So she conceived him, and withdrew with him to a remote place.﴾

﴿So she conceived him, and withdrew with him to a remote place.﴾ That is: when she became pregnant with him, she secluded herself, because of him, in a distant place away from her people, fleeing from the gossip (al-qalah). It has been related from the early generations (al-salaf) that when Gabriel spoke to her on behalf of God, exalted is He, with what he said, of what has preceded, she submitted to the decree of God, exalted is He, and was reassured by his words.

Then he approached her and breathed into the opening of her shirt (jayb dir'ihā). The breath travelled until it entered the womb (al-farj), and she conceived by God's leave, exalted is He.

The discussion on the interpretation of His words, exalted is He:

[23] ﴿So the pains of childbirth drove her to the trunk of the palm tree. She said, "Oh, I wish I had died before this and had been a thing forgotten, utterly forgotten."﴾

﴿So the pains of childbirth drove her to the trunk of the palm tree﴾, i.e., the pain of labour compelled her to lean against the trunk, so that she might rely on it and shelter herself with it. (p-٤١٣٤) Al-Zamakhshari said that "ajā'a" (drove, compelled) is derived from "jā'a" (came), but its usage changed after the transitive form to mean "compelling." It is also read as "al-mikhāḍ" (with a kasra on the mīm). Both are verbal nouns of "makhadat al-mar'ah" (the woman went into labour), when the child moves in her womb to come out. ﴿She said, "Oh, I wish I had died before this"﴾, i.e., before this pregnancy. ﴿and had been a thing forgotten, utterly forgotten﴾, i.e., something trivial, whose nature is to be forgotten and not regarded. "Mansiyyan" means one that does not come to anyone's mind; it is an intensive adjective. She said this because she knew that she would be afflicted and tested through this child, whom people would not judge fairly regarding her affair. Thus there came over her great shame and fear of blame, if they accused her while she knew her innocence and the opposite of what she had been slandered with, namely that God had singled her out with the utmost honour and favour. Al-Zamakhshari said: because it is a slippery position, on which feet rarely remain firm, that you recognise your own joy at a great matter and an outstanding grace, which makes you deserving of praise and entitled to honour, and then you see that people, because of their ignorance of it, consider it a fault for which you are blamed and reproached.

The discussion of His words, exalted is He:

[24] ﴿So he called to her from beneath her: "Do not grieve, for your Lord has provided a stream beneath you."﴾

﴿So he called to her from beneath her﴾ — i.e., from a place lower than her, beneath a mound; and it was Jibril (Gabriel). It has also been said that it was ʿIsā (Jesus). And it was read as (man) with a fatha on the mim, as a relative pronoun: ﴿"Do not grieve, for your Lord has provided beneath you a sariyy"﴾ — i.e., a noble, elevated lord (sayyid); and it has been said: a flowing stream (nahr yasri).

The discussion on the interpretation (ta'wil) of His saying, exalted is He:

[25] ﴿And shake toward yourself the trunk of the palm tree; it will drop upon you fresh ripe dates.﴾

﴿And shake toward yourself the trunk of the palm tree; it will drop upon you fresh ripe dates.﴾ Meaning: the time for picking it has arrived. Al-Zamakhshari said: If you say, "Her grief was not over the lack of food and drink, so that she would be consoled by the stream and the dates!" I say: The consolation was not through them insofar as they are food and drink, but insofar as they are two miracles that show the people that she is among those protected from sin, far from suspicion, and that someone like her is far removed from what they accused her of. And that for her there are divine matters outside of customary habits, breaking what they had become accustomed to and familiar with, so that it becomes clear to them that her giving birth without a male is not a novelty in her case.

The discussion on the interpretation of His words, exalted is He:

[26] ﴿So eat and drink, and let your eye be cooled. And if you see any human being, say: "I have vowed a fast to the Most Merciful, so I will not speak to any human today."﴾

﴿So eat and drink, and let your eye be cooled﴾: that is, with perfection and with a blessed child, brought into existence by power and bestowed by care. Al-Zamakhshari said: That is, We have combined for you two benefits in the stream and the dates: the first is eating and drinking, and the second is the consolation of the heart, because they are two miracles. This is the meaning of His words: ﴿So eat and drink, and let your eye be cooled﴾, that is, be content of soul and do not grieve. Cast off from yourself whatever saddens and troubles you. ﴿And if you see any human being﴾, that is, among those veiled from the realities by the outward appearances of causes, who do not understand your words and do not believe your condition, because they cling to custom and are veiled from the light of truth. ﴿Then say: "I have vowed a fast to the Most Merciful, so I will not speak to any human today."﴾, that is, do not speak to them about your affair at all, and do not persist with them in what they cannot accept. She was commanded to do this only because of her dislike of arguing with fools, and to be satisfied with the speech of Jesus, peace be upon him, for it is a decisive proof of her innocence. Commentary of al-Qasimi (Mahasin al-Ta'wil) on surah 19, verse 27:

The discussion of the interpretation of His words, exalted is He:

[27] ﴿Then she brought him to her people, carrying him. They said, "O Mary, you have certainly come with something monstrous."﴾

﴿Then she brought him to her people, carrying him. They said, "O Mary, you have certainly come with something monstrous."﴾ That is: something great and abhorrent.

[28] ﴿O sister of Aaron, your father was not a man of evil, nor was your mother an unchaste woman.﴾

﴿O sister of Aaron, your father was not a man of evil, nor was your mother an unchaste woman.﴾ This is a resumed statement, serving to renew the reproach, to emphasize the rebuke, and to affirm that what she brought was an enormity (fariyy). Harun (Aaron) is the well-known Prophet, may the blessings of Allah be upon him. They mean that she is like him in righteousness, because "brother" and "sister" are frequently used in the sense of one who resembles another.

The discussion of the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

[29] ﴿So she pointed to him. They said, "How can we speak to one who is in the cradle, a young child?"﴾

﴿So she pointed to him. They said﴾, disapproving of her response: ﴿"How can we speak to one who is in the cradle, a young child?"﴾ For it was not known for a sensible person to speak to a child in the cradle.

**The interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:**

﴿And dutiful to my mother, and He has not made me an arrogant wretch.﴾ That is, one who is haughty toward His obedience and His command.

﴿And peace be upon me the day I was born, and the day I die, and the day I am raised alive.﴾ ﴿That﴾ [Maryam 19:34], that is, the one whose sublime attributes and striking qualities have been detailed: ﴿Isa son of Maryam﴾, that is, not what the Christians ascribe to him. This is a refutation of them, in their claims, in the most eloquent manner and with a demonstrative method, since He described him with the opposites of what they attribute to him: ﴿a word of truth about which they dispute﴾ [19:34]. ﴿It is not for Allah to take a son; glory be to Him. When He decrees a matter, He only says to it, "Be," and it is﴾ [19:35]. That is, how can it be imagined that one with such a condition should have a son?

This is like His saying: ﴿Indeed, the likeness of Isa before Allah is like the likeness of Adam. He created him from dust, then said to him, "Be," and he was﴾ [Al 'Imran 3:59]. ﴿The truth is from your Lord, so do not be among the doubters﴾ [3:60]. Then He pointed to the completion of Isa's speech, in commanding the worship of Him alone, with His saying: ﴿And indeed, Allah is my Lord and your Lord, so worship Him. This is a straight path﴾ [19:36], that is, upright. Whoever follows it is guided and rightly guided, and whoever opposes it goes astray and errs.

**Remarks on the benefits of this story:**

The first: When He mentioned the story of Zakariyya, peace be upon him, and that He brought forth from him, in his old age and his wife's barrenness, a pure, blessed, righteous son, He followed it with the story of Maryam in bringing forth her son Isa from her without a father, peace be upon them both. There is a correspondence and resemblance between the two stories. For this reason He mentioned both in Al 'Imran, here, and in Surat al-Anbiya'. He links the two stories because of the closeness of their meanings, to show His servants His power and the greatness of His dominion, and that He is capable of whatever He wills. Maryam is the daughter of 'Imran, from a pure, good household among the Children of Israel. Allah mentioned her mother's giving birth to her in Surat Al 'Imran, that her mother vowed her as dedicated to worship, that her Lord accepted her with a good acceptance and caused her to grow in a good growth, so she grew up among the Children of Israel in a great upbringing, and became one of the devout women who devoted themselves wholly to worship. She was under the guardianship of Zakariyya, who saw in her such marvels that they dazzled him, for whenever he entered upon her in the sanctuary (mihrab) he would find provision with her, as was mentioned earlier in Surat Al 'Imran.

The second: Whoever said that Maryam was a prophetess cited His saying: ﴿Then We sent to her Our Spirit﴾ [19:17]. It was also cited, regarding her, His saying: ﴿O, would that I had died before this﴾ [19:23], as evidence for the permissibility of wishing for death in such a state. And His saying: ﴿And shake toward you the trunk of the palm tree﴾ [19:25], as evidence for taking the means to obtain provision and exerting effort in earning. The poet alluded to this:

*Did you not see that Allah said to Maryam: "And shake toward you the trunk, and fresh dates will fall upon you"?*
*Had He willed, He could have bent the trunk toward her without her shaking it, but everything has its cause.*

In the verse is a basis for what physicians say: that fresh dates benefit women. It was also cited, with His saying after: ﴿So she pointed to him﴾ [19:29], following: ﴿So I will never speak today to any human being﴾ [19:26], as evidence that one who swears not to speak to or address so-and-so does not break his oath by gesturing. And as evidence that keeping silent before a foolish person is obligatory, as az-Zamakhshari deduced, saying:

*Whoever humiliates people is a fool, and finds no one to match his foolishness.*

In His saying: ﴿Your father was not a man of evil﴾ [19:28] is the meaning of their proverb: "Whoever resembles his father has not wronged." It also contains a warning that committing abominations by the children of righteous people is more abominable.

The third: Ar-Razi quoted from al-Qadi regarding His saying: ﴿And peace be upon me﴾ [19:33], etc., that peace (salam) is an expression for what brings about security, and from it comes soundness in blessings and the removal of calamities. So it is as if he asked his Lord and requested what Allah, exalted is He, mentioned as His action toward Yahya. Prophets must be those whose supplications are answered. The most vital states in which a human being needs soundness are these three conditions: the day of birth, the day of death, and the day of resurrection. So all the states in which one needs soundness and the gathering of happiness, he asked from Him, exalted is He, so that he would be protected from calamities and transgressions in every state.

The fourth: Al-Qashani said: He only appeared to her as a human being of sound character and good form, so that her soul would be affected by him and find comfort. Thus her nature would be moved according to its natural disposition, and the effect would flow from the imagination into the physical nature, so her desire would be stirred and she would descend, as happens in a dream with nocturnal emission, and her seed would be ejected into the womb, and the child is formed from it. It has been mentioned that revelation is close to true dreams, because of the quiescence of the bodily power and its inactivity in its functions during it, as in sleep. Thus whatever is seen in the imagination of the states that come upon the rational soul, which in our terminology is called the heart (qalb), and the connections it has with the holy spirits, flows into the animal and natural soul, and the body is affected by it. The generation of a child from a single drop became possible because it is established in the natural sciences that the male's semen in the formation of the child is like rennet in cheese, and the female's semen is like milk. That is, the setting (ʿaqd) comes from the male's semen, and the coagulation (inʿiqad) comes from the female's semen. This does not mean that the male's semen alone holds the coagulating power and the female's semen alone holds the coagulated power, but that the coagulating power in the male's semen is stronger, and the coagulated power in the female's semen is stronger. Otherwise they could not unite into one thing, and the male's semen would not coagulate until it becomes part of the child. Accordingly, if (p-٤١٤٠) the temperament of the female is strongly masculine, as is the temperament of noble women of strong faculties, and the temperament of her liver is hot, the semen separated from her right kidney would be much hotter than that separated from her left kidney. When they come together in the womb, and the temperament of the womb is strong in retention and attraction, the one separated in the right kidney takes the place of the male in the intensity of its strength in binding, and the one separated from the left kidney takes the place of the female's semen in the strength of coagulation, and the child is formed. Especially if the soul is supported by the Holy Spirit and strengthened, the effect of its connection with it flows into the nature and the body, changes the temperament, and extends all faculties in their actions with spiritual extension, so it becomes more capable in its actions in ways that cannot be governed by measure. And Allah knows best.

Then he said regarding His saying: ﴿And it was a matter decreed﴾ [19:21], that it was predetermined in the Preserved Tablet from eternity. And from Ibn 'Abbas: she was reassured by his saying: ﴿I am only a messenger of your Lord, to give you a pure son﴾ [19:19]. So he drew near to her and breathed into the slit of the garment, that is, the body. This was the cause of her emission, as we have mentioned, like sexual excitement, for example, and embracing, which often becomes a cause of emission. It was said: the Spirit that appeared to her is the spirit of Isa, peace be upon him, at his descent, and his connection with her and his attachment to her semen. The truth is that it is the Holy Spirit, because it was the efficient cause of his existence, as He said: ﴿to give you a pure son﴾ [19:19]. The connection of the spirit of Isa with the semen occurs only after the semen has come into the womb and settled there, until it mixes, unites, and receives a temperament suitable for receiving the spirit. End of quote.

The fifth: Tamaththul (taking a form) is derived from mithl (likeness), and its meaning is imagining. In it is evidence that the angel takes the form of a human being.

Imam al-Haramayn (al-Juwayni) said: The angel Jibril's taking a form means that Allah annihilated or removed the surplus of his creation, and did not return it to him afterward.

Ibn 'Abd al-Salam asserted removal without annihilation, and established this by saying that the departure of the soul need not cause his death, but it is permissible that it remain in the body alive, because the death of the body by the separation of the soul is not rationally necessary, but is by a custom that Allah, exalted is He, has established in some of His creation. A parallel is the transfer of the souls of martyrs into the bellies of green birds that roam in Paradise.

Al-Balqini said: What Imam al-Haramayn mentioned does not confine the matter to it. It is possible that the one who came was Jibril in his original form, but it was condensed so that it became the size of a man's form, and when it leaves that, it returns to its own form. An example of this is cotton: when it is gathered after having been fluffed, by fluffing it takes on a large appearance, though its essence has not changed. This is by way of approximation. The truth is that an angel's taking the form of a man does not mean that his essence transformed into a man, but that he appeared in that form to comfort the one he addresses. The apparent matter is also that the surplus does not vanish or perish, but is only hidden from the viewer. And Allah knows best. Thus said Ibn Hajar in Fath al-Bari.

It is not hidden that this discussion is of conjecturing about the unseen and pursuing what one does not comprehend. Plunging into it is vain, and its plunger ends where he began. For it belongs to the realm of the unseen, which our knowledge does not reach and will never reach by reason alone. No decisive text has come from the Infallible (ﷺ) regarding it, and whatever is of this kind is not for us to investigate. So know this, for it will benefit you in many places.

The sixth: Some of them said: The original of the word ʿIsa is Yasu'. The Jews altered it to ʿAysu, mockingly, and the Arabs changed it to ʿIsa, making it resemble the name Musa. The substitution of the waw by the alif has a cause based on the rules of the Hebrew language, and indeed of Arabic. End of quote.

The fourth: Al-Qashani said: He only appeared to her as a human being of sound character and good form, so that her soul would be affected by him and find comfort. Thus her nature would be moved according to its natural disposition, and the effect would flow from the imagination into the physical nature, so her desire would be stirred and she would descend, as happens in a dream with nocturnal emission, and her seed would be ejected into the womb, and the child is formed from it. It has been mentioned that revelation is close to true dreams, because of the quiescence of the bodily power and its inactivity in its functions during it, as in sleep. Thus whatever is seen in the imagination of the states that come upon the rational soul, which in our terminology is called the heart (qalb), and the connections it has with the holy spirits, flows into the animal and natural soul, and the body is affected by it. The generation of a child from a single drop became possible because it is established in the natural sciences that the male's semen in the formation of the child is like rennet in cheese, and the female's semen is like milk. That is, the setting (ʿaqd) comes from the male's semen, and the coagulation (inʿiqad) comes from the female's semen. This does not mean that the male's semen alone holds the coagulating power and the female's semen alone holds the coagulated power, but that the coagulating power in the male's semen is stronger, and the coagulated power in the female's semen is stronger. Otherwise they could not unite into one thing, and the male's semen would not coagulate until it becomes part of the child. Accordingly, if (p-٤١٤٠) the temperament of the female is strongly masculine, as is the temperament of noble women of strong faculties, and the temperament of her liver is hot, the semen separated from her right kidney would be much hotter than that separated from her left kidney. When they come together in the womb, and the temperament of the womb is strong in retention and attraction, the one separated in the right kidney takes the place of the male in the intensity of its strength in binding, and the one separated from the left kidney takes the place of the female's semen in the strength of coagulation, and the child is formed. Especially if the soul is supported by the Holy Spirit and strengthened, the effect of its connection with it flows into the nature and the body, changes the temperament, and extends all faculties in their actions with spiritual extension, so it becomes more capable in its actions in ways that cannot be governed by measure. And Allah knows best.

Then he said regarding His saying: ﴿And it was a matter decreed﴾ [19:21], that it was predetermined in the Preserved Tablet from eternity. And from Ibn 'Abbas: she was reassured by his saying: ﴿I am only a messenger of your Lord, to give you a pure son﴾ [19:19]. So he drew near to her and breathed into the slit of the garment, that is, the body. This was the cause of her emission, as we have mentioned, like sexual excitement, for example, and embracing, which often becomes a cause of emission. It was said: the Spirit that appeared to her is the spirit of Isa, peace be upon him, at his descent, and his connection with her and his attachment to her semen. The truth is that it is the Holy Spirit, because it was the efficient cause of his existence, as He said: ﴿to give you a pure son﴾ [19:19]. The connection of the spirit of Isa with the semen occurs only after the semen has come into the womb and settled there, until it mixes, unites, and receives a temperament suitable for receiving the spirit. End of quote.

The fifth: Tamaththul (taking a form) is derived from mithl (likeness), and its meaning is imagining. In it is evidence that the angel takes the form of a human being.

Imam al-Haramayn (al-Juwayni) said: The angel Jibril's taking a form means that Allah annihilated or removed the surplus of his creation, and did not return it to him afterward.

Ibn 'Abd al-Salam asserted removal without annihilation, and established this by saying that the departure of the soul need not cause his death, but it is permissible that it remain in the body alive, because the death of the body by the separation of the soul is not rationally necessary, but is by a custom that Allah, exalted is He, has established in some of His creation. A parallel is the transfer of the souls of martyrs into the bellies of green birds that roam in Paradise.

Al-Balqini said: What Imam al-Haramayn mentioned does not confine the matter to it. It is possible that the one who came was Jibril in his original form, but it was condensed so that it became the size of a man's form, and when it leaves that, it returns to its own form. An example of this is cotton: when it is gathered after having been fluffed, by fluffing it takes on a large appearance, though its essence has not changed. This is by way of approximation. The truth is that an angel's taking the form of a man does not mean that his essence transformed into a man, but that he appeared in that form to comfort the one he addresses. The apparent matter is also that the surplus does not vanish or perish, but is only hidden from the viewer. And Allah knows best. Thus said Ibn Hajar in Fath al-Bari.

It is not hidden that this discussion is of conjecturing about the unseen and pursuing what one does not comprehend. Plunging into it is vain, and its plunger ends where he began. For it belongs to the realm of the unseen, which our knowledge does not reach and will never reach by reason alone. No decisive text has come from the Infallible (ﷺ) regarding it, and whatever is of this kind is not for us to investigate. So know this, for it will benefit you in many places.

The sixth: Some of them said: The original of the word ʿIsa is Yasu'. The Jews altered it to ʿAysu, mockingly, and the Arabs changed it to ʿIsa, making it resemble the name Musa. The substitution of the waw by the alif has a cause based on the rules of the Hebrew language, and indeed of Arabic. End of quote.

The discourse on the interpretation of His words, exalted is He:

[37] ﴿Then the factions differed among themselves, so woe to those who disbelieved, from the scene of a tremendous day.﴾

﴿Then the factions differed among themselves﴾ meaning: the People of the Book differed in their statements about ʿĪsā (Jesus), after his matter had been made clear (p-4142) and his condition had become evident, namely that he is God's servant and messenger, His word which He cast to Maryam (Mary), and a spirit from Him. The Jews among them persisted in slandering his mother and accusing him of sorcery. The Christians split over his affair into divisions beyond counting, and all of it is misguidance, polytheism, and disbelief. But God guided those who believed to the truth concerning which they differed, by His permission. This is from His grace and bounty, exalted is He: ﴿so woe to those who disbelieved, from the scene of a tremendous day﴾, meaning by "those who disbelieved" the differing parties. He expressed them by the relative form (alladhīna) to signal that they all share in disbelief and to indicate the reason for the ruling.

As for (mashhad), there are six possibilities. It is either a mīmī verbal noun, or a noun of time or of place. In every case it derives either from (al-shuhūd), meaning presence, or from (al-shahādah), meaning testimony. This is the sense of al-Zamakhsharī's statement: that is, in their witnessing the terror of the reckoning and the recompense until the Day of Resurrection. Or it is from the place of witnessing, which is the standing place. Or from the time of witnessing. Or from the testimony of that day against them, and that the angels, the prophets, their tongues, their hands, and their feet bear witness against them for their disbelief and evil deeds. Or it is from the place of testimony or its time.

It has been said: its meaning is what they testified to concerning ʿĪsā and his mother, and He magnified it because of the magnitude of what is in it as well, like His saying: ﴿Grave is the word that comes out of their mouths﴾ [al-Kahf: 5]. In it is a threat for them and a severe warning. This is because there is no one more wrongdoing than one who denies the truth when it has come to him.

And His saying, exalted is He:

Commentary of al-Qasimi (Mahasin al-Ta'wil) on surah 19, verse 38:

The discussion on the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

[38] ﴿Hear them and see them, on the Day they come to Us! But the wrongdoers today are in clear error.﴾

﴿Hear them and see them, on the Day they come to Us!﴾ is an expression of wonder at the keenness of their hearing and their sight on that Day. Its meaning is that their hearing and their sight, on the Day they come to Us for reckoning and recompense, are deserving of being wondered at, after they had been deaf and blind in the world. The verse is like His saying, exalted is He: ﴿If only you could see when the guilty will hang their heads before their Lord, [saying], "Our Lord, we have seen and we have heard"﴾ [al-Sajdah: 12], and so on, meaning: they say that when it no longer benefits them at all. Had this been said before witnessing the punishment, it would have been of benefit. ﴿But the wrongdoers today﴾ meaning: in the world ﴿are in clear error﴾ (p-4143) because of their neglect of hearing and looking. Therefore, when guidance is asked of them, they are not guided. Al-Zamakhshari said: He placed the apparent noun, I mean (the wrongdoers), in the position of the pronoun, to indicate that there is no wrong greater than their wrong, in that they neglected hearing and looking at the time when it would have benefited them and made them happy.

Note:

The wonder in the verse was interpreted in the manner mentioned, and that it is directed at the servants from whom wonder proceeds, because its proceeding from God, exalted is He, is impossible. For it is a psychological state that arises from magnifying something whose cause is not known. Hence it is said: when the cause becomes apparent, wonder ceases. The meaning is: they wondered at their hearing and their sight, since that benefits them not. It is like His saying, exalted is He: ﴿So We removed from you your covering, and today your sight is sharp﴾ [Qaf: 22]. This was stated by al-Shihab.

This is the method of the theologians (mutakallimun) in interpreting those attributes transmitted that are attributed both to God, exalted is He, and to His creation. The method of the verified early scholars (al-Salaf al-Muhaqqiqun) is affirming what revelation has stated while negating resemblance (tashbih), for there is no commonality between the attributes of the Creator and the attributes of the created. What is attributed to Him, exalted is He, is in the manner that befits His majesty. Whatever attributes are conceived for created beings that entail impossibility do not necessarily have to entail that for Him, exalted is He. Just as knowledge, power, hearing, sight and speech in us entail deficiency and need, from which God must be declared free, so too existence and self-subsistence in us entail need for a Creator who makes us exist. God is exalted in His existence above what our existence needs. We, our attributes and our actions are bound up with need of other than ourselves. Need is an intrinsic matter for us that cannot be separated from us. He, glorified is He, the Self-Sufficient, has an intrinsic matter that cannot be separated from Him. He is by Himself Living, Self-Subsisting, Necessarily Existent, while we by ourselves are needy and poor. So if our essence, attributes, actions, and the perfection we are characterized by, such as knowledge, power and other things, are bound up with need, contingency and createdness, it does not follow that God has no essence, attributes or actions, and that He has no power and no knowledge, because that would entail need as it does in us. Likewise, every attribute brought by revelation, if it is supposed that in our case it entails need and weakness, it does not follow that it must entail that for God, exalted is He. This is what Imam Taqi al-Din Ibn Taymiyyah established in the course of some of his fatwas. His words here serve as a general principle for matters of this kind. So memorise it.

The discourse on the interpretation of His words, exalted is He:

[39] ﴿And warn them of the Day of Regret, when the matter will have been decided, while they are in heedlessness and do not believe.﴾ [40] ﴿Indeed, We inherit the earth and whoever is upon it, and to Us they will be returned.﴾ [Maryam: 39–40].

﴿And warn them of the Day of Regret, when the matter will have been decided﴾ i.e., the reckoning will have been completed, the people of Paradise will have been separated from the people of the Fire, and each party will have gone to what it has gone to, abiding therein eternally. ﴿While they are in heedlessness﴾ i.e., they are now immersed in heedlessness of what will be done to them in the Hereafter. ﴿And they do not believe﴾ i.e., they do not affirm it today, though they will witness it. Then Exalted God commanded His Messenger to recite to them the story of Ibrahim (Abraham), because they trace their lineage to him, so that they might take a lesson from his pure monotheism. So He, glorified is He, said:

The discourse on the interpretation of His words, exalted is He:

[39] ﴿And warn them of the Day of Regret, when the matter will have been decided, while they are in heedlessness and do not believe.﴾ [40] ﴿Indeed, We inherit the earth and whoever is upon it, and to Us they will be returned.﴾ [Maryam: 39–40].

﴿And warn them of the Day of Regret, when the matter will have been decided﴾ i.e., the reckoning will have been completed, the people of Paradise will have been separated from the people of the Fire, and each party will have gone to what it has gone to, abiding therein eternally. ﴿While they are in heedlessness﴾ i.e., they are now immersed in heedlessness of what will be done to them in the Hereafter. ﴿And they do not believe﴾ i.e., they do not affirm it today, though they will witness it. Then Exalted God commanded His Messenger to recite to them the story of Ibrahim (Abraham), because they trace their lineage to him, so that they might take a lesson from his pure monotheism. So He, glorified is He, said:

The discussion on the interpretation of His, the Exalted, saying:

[41] ﴿And mention in the Book Abraham. Indeed, he was a man of truth and a prophet.﴾ [42] ﴿When he said to his father, "O my father, why do you worship that which does not hear and does not see and cannot benefit you at all?"﴾ [Maryam: 42].

﴿And mention in the Book Abraham. Indeed, he was a man of truth﴾, one of intense affirmation of what is due to God of divine oneness (tawhid) and transcendence (tanzih). ﴿A prophet﴾. ﴿When he said to his father﴾ [Maryam: 42], meaning: gently in his call to monotheism and his prohibition of worshipping idols. ﴿"O my father, why do you worship that which does not hear and does not see and cannot benefit you at all"﴾ [Maryam: 42], meaning: it does not repel harm nor bring benefit.

Abu al-Su'ud said: Peace be upon him followed in his call the most excellent method and the most upright path, and argued against him (p-4145) with the most wondrous argument, with good manners and a beautiful character, so that he would not ride the back of obstinacy and stubbornness, nor fall entirely away from the path of guidance. He asked him for the reason for his worship of that which every intelligent person's reason, whether learned or ignorant, finds contemptible and refuses to accept, let alone worship it, which is the ultimate extreme of veneration, while such worship is only fitting for one who has complete self-sufficiency and all-encompassing bounty: the Creator, the Provider, the Giver of life, the Giver of death, the Rewarder, the Punisher. He also drew attention to the fact that the intelligent person must do everything he does for a sound motive and a sound purpose. Even if the thing were living, discerning, hearing, seeing, able to benefit and harm, capable of bringing good and evil, it would still be possible that a sound intellect would disdain to worship it, even if it were the noblest of creatures, because it sees its like in need and in submission to the compelling, necessary power. So what do you think of an inanimate object made of stone or wood, which has no attribute of living things, neither trace nor sign?

The discussion on the interpretation (ta'wil) of His saying, exalted is He:

[43] ﴿O my father, indeed there has come to me of knowledge what has not come to you, so follow me; I will guide you to a balanced path.﴾

﴿O my father, indeed there has come to me of knowledge what has not come to you﴾ That is: the right of the one who is lacking (al-qasir) is to follow the perfect person (al-insan al-kamil). ﴿So follow me; I will guide you to a balanced path﴾, that is, a moderate path (mu'tadilan), with no excess (ifrat) in worshipping what does not deserve worship, and no neglect (tafrit) in abandoning the worship of what deserves it, and likewise in matters of character and deeds. Al-Mahayimi said: That is, even though it is customary for the son's right to be to follow his father, that is false, because the right is to follow what is correct.

Al-Zamakhshari said: Peace be upon him followed up with his call to the truth, being gentle and kind toward him. He did not describe his father with extreme ignorance, nor himself with superior knowledge. Rather, he said: Indeed, with me is a portion of knowledge and something of it that is not with you, and that is the knowledge of guidance to the straight way. So do not be proud. Suppose that you and I are on a journey, and I have knowledge of the guidance that you do not have; then follow me, and I will save you from going astray and wandering.

Commentary of al-Qasimi (Mahasin al-Ta'wil) on surah 19, verse 44:

(p-4146) The discussion on the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

[44] ﴿O my father, do not worship Satan. Indeed, Satan has been disobedient to the Most Merciful.﴾

﴿O my father, do not worship Satan. Indeed, Satan has been disobedient to the Most Merciful.﴾ He (peace be upon him) gave him a gentle admonition and forbade him from what he was upon, by depicting it in a form that every rational person would find repugnant, and by explaining that it, despite being utterly devoid of benefit, draws in a great harm, for in reality it is the worship of Satan, since he is the one who commands it and makes it attractive to him. His saying, ﴿Indeed, Satan﴾ and so on, is a justification for the reason behind the prohibition and a reinforcement of it, by explaining that he is defiant toward your Lord, who has bestowed upon you countless blessings. There is no doubt that whoever obeys a disobedient one is himself disobedient. The use of the explicit noun in place of the pronoun is for the sake of greater emphasis. Singling out his disobedience from among all his other crimes is because it is the foundation of them. And the mention of the title "the Most Merciful" is to highlight the utter enormity of his disobedience. This was related by Abu al-Su'ud.

The discussion on the interpretation of His, the Exalted, saying:

﴿O my father, indeed I fear that a punishment from the Most Merciful will touch you, so you would become a companion of Satan.﴾

﴿O my father, indeed I fear that a punishment from the Most Merciful will touch you﴾ because you have disobeyed Him and allied yourself with His enemy, so He will cut off His mercy from you, just as He cut it off from Satan. ﴿So you would become a companion of Satan﴾, meaning: an associate of his and a sharer with him in his punishment.

Al-Zamakhshari said: He (peace be upon him) went about it with a measured approach in warning him of the evil outcome and of what his present state would lead to in terms of consequence and ruin. This was not without good manners, for he did not state outright that the punishment was due to him or that torment was certainly attached to him. Instead he said: ﴿I fear that a punishment will touch you﴾, mentioning fear and touching, and leaving the punishment indefinite. He made Satan's guardianship and his entry into the company of Satan's followers and allies greater than the punishment itself. And he opened each of the four pieces of advice with the words ﴿O my father﴾, seeking his favor and winning his compassion.

(p-4147)The discussion of the interpretation of His words, may He be exalted:

[46] ﴿He said: "Do you turn away from my gods, O Ibrahim? If you do not desist, I will surely stone you, so leave me alone for a long time."﴾

﴿He said﴾ — that is, his father, insisting on his obstinacy because of his extreme excess in error: ﴿"Do you turn away from my gods, O Ibrahim?"﴾ — that is, "Are you averse to them and turning away from them?" He placed the predicate before the subject because it was more important to him. He introduced it with the interrogative hamza to deny the very act of turning away, in a manner of astonishment, as if turning away from them were something that could not proceed from a rational person, let alone encouraging others to turn away from them. In this there is consolation for the Messenger, may the blessings of Allah be upon him, for what he suffered from the like of this from the disbelievers of his people.

His words, ﴿"If you do not desist, I will surely stone you"﴾, are a threat of the utmost severity — that is, "If you do not desist from speaking against them and from your advice, I will surely stone you with stones." ﴿"So leave me alone for a long time"﴾ — that is, "Keep away from me for a long period of time."

The commentary of al-Qasimi (Mahasin al-Ta'wil) on surah 19, verse 47:

The discussion of the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

[47] ﴿He said, "Peace be upon you. I will ask forgiveness for you from my Lord. Indeed, He has ever been to me Most Gracious."﴾

﴿He said, "Peace be upon you. I will ask forgiveness for you from my Lord. Indeed, He has ever been to me Most Gracious."﴾ That is: extremely kind to me. In his reply, with his saying (peace be upon him): ﴿Peace be upon you﴾ is the repaying of an evil deed with a good one, as God the Exalted said: ﴿And when the ignorant address them, they say, "Peace"﴾ [al-Furqan: 63], meaning: I will not harm you with anything disagreeable from now on. But I will supplicate my Lord that He forgive you, as He said: ﴿And forgive my father﴾ [al-Shu'ara': 86]. Al-Zamakhshari said: In the verse is evidence for the permissibility of forsaking the one being advised, when the situation is this. It is also possible that he prayed for him for safety, seeking to win him over. Do you not see that he promised him forgiveness?

In (al-Iklil): Some scholars used the verse as evidence for the permissibility of initiating greeting (salam) to a disbeliever.

Ibn Kathir said: Abraham (peace be upon him) asked forgiveness for his father for a long time, and after he migrated to the Levant and built the Sacred Mosque, and after Isma'il and Isaac were born to him, in his saying: ﴿Our Lord, forgive me and my parents and the believers on the day the reckoning is established﴾ [Ibrahim: 41]. And the Muslims asked forgiveness for their relatives and families among the polytheists at the beginning of Islam, following Abraham the Friend (khalil) in that. Until God the Exalted revealed: ﴿There has already been for you an excellent example in Abraham and those with him, when they said to their people, "Indeed, we are free of you and whatever you worship other than God"﴾ [al-Mumtahanah: 4], up to His saying: ﴿except for the saying of Abraham to his father, "I will surely ask forgiveness for you"﴾ [al-Mumtahanah: 4], meaning: except in this statement, so do not take him as an example in it.

Then Allah explained that Ibrahim desisted from that and turned away from it. So Allah the Exalted said: ﴿It is not for the Prophet and those who believe to seek forgiveness for the polytheists﴾ [at-Tawbah: 113], up to His words: ﴿And the seeking of forgiveness by Ibrahim for his father was only because of a promise he had made to him. But when it became clear to him that he was an enemy to Allah, he disassociated himself from him. Indeed, Ibrahim was compassionate and forbearing﴾ [at-Tawbah: 114]. And His saying:

The discussion on the interpretation of His saying, the Exalted:

[48] ﴿And I will remove myself from you and from what you invoke besides Allah, and I will invoke my Lord. Perhaps I will not be in invoking my Lord unhappy.﴾

﴿And I will remove myself from you﴾ means: I will distance myself from you and from your people by migration. ﴿And what you invoke besides Allah﴾ means: from your idols.

Az-Zamakhshari said: The intended meaning of "invocation" (ad-du'a') is worship ('ibadah), because it is part of it and one of its means. From this is His Messenger's (ﷺ) saying: "Supplication is worship." And His saying, the Exalted, supports this: ﴿So when he had removed himself from them and what they worshipped besides Allah﴾ [Maryam: 49]. (p-4149) ﴿And I will invoke my Lord﴾ means: I will worship Him alone. ﴿Perhaps I will not be in invoking my Lord unhappy﴾ means: disappointed, with my effort lost. In this there is an allusion to their wretchedness through invoking their gods, together with humility before Allah through the word "perhaps" ('asa), and what it contains of self-abasement, observance of good manners, and an indication that answering and rewarding come by way of Allah's grace.

The discussion of His saying, may He be exalted:

[49] ﴿So when he withdrew from them and from what they worshipped besides Allah, We gave him Isaac and Jacob, and We made each of them a prophet.﴾

﴿So when he withdrew from them and from what they worshipped besides Allah﴾ — and that was by his emigration to the Levant (al-Sham). ﴿We gave him Isaac and Jacob, and We made each of them a prophet﴾ — i.e., We made for him sons and grandsons (hafadah), prophets, in whom his eye was comforted during his lifetime, in place of those among his relatives, the disbelievers and the wicked, whom he had parted from.

And His saying, Exalted is He:

The discussion on the interpretation of His saying, Exalted is He:

[50] ﴿And We bestowed upon them of Our mercy and made for them a tongue of truth, high.﴾

﴿And We bestowed upon them of Our mercy﴾ That is: what was known among them of prophethood (nubuwwah), offspring, abundance of provision, and possession of the Holy Land. ﴿And We made for them a tongue of truth, high﴾ That is: good praise. He expressed by "tongue" what is found through the tongue, just as He expressed by "hand" what is applied to the hand, which is a gift. Its being attributed to truth and described as high serves to indicate that they deserve what is praised of them, and that their striving is not hidden.

Commentary of al-Qasimi (Mahasin al-Ta'wil) on surah 19, verses 51–52:

The discussion of the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

[51] ﴿And mention in the Book Moses. Indeed, he was chosen, and he was a messenger and a prophet.﴾ [52] ﴿And We called him from the right side of the mount and brought him near in confidence.﴾ [Maryam: 51–52].

﴿And mention in the Book Moses. Indeed, he was chosen﴾ with the letter lam pronounced with a kasra (mukhlisan, meaning): he made his worship sincere (ikhlas), free of association (shirk), and submitted his face to Allah. It has also been recited with a fatha (mukhlasan), meaning: Allah made him sincere, that is, chose him (istafahu), as He said: ﴿I have chosen you above the people﴾ [al-A'raf: 144]. ﴿And he was a messenger and a prophet.﴾ ﴿And We called him from the right side of the mount﴾ [Maryam: 52], that is, from its right side, from the perspective of Moses, when he went seeking a brand from that fire, and he saw it shining, so he headed toward it and found it there. Then he was called at that place. ﴿And We brought him near in confidence﴾ [Maryam: 52], that is, one who converses in secret (munajiyan), meaning one spoken to (kalim), for We spoke to him without an intermediary.

Commentary of al-Qasimi (Mahasin al-Ta'wil) on surah 19, verses 51–52:

The discussion of the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

[51] ﴿And mention in the Book Moses. Indeed, he was chosen, and he was a messenger and a prophet.﴾ [52] ﴿And We called him from the right side of the mount and brought him near in confidence.﴾ [Maryam: 51–52].

﴿And mention in the Book Moses. Indeed, he was chosen﴾ with the letter lam pronounced with a kasra (mukhlisan, meaning): he made his worship sincere (ikhlas), free of association (shirk), and submitted his face to Allah. The discussion of the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

[53] ﴿And We gave him, out of Our mercy, his brother Harun as a prophet﴾.

﴿And We gave him, out of Our mercy, his brother Harun as a prophet﴾, so that he might strengthen his arm (i.e., support him) in conveying the message.

The discourse on the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

[54] ﴿And mention in the Book Ismail. Indeed, he was true to his promise, and he was a messenger and a prophet.﴾ [55] ﴿And he used to enjoin on his family prayer and zakah, and he was pleasing to his Lord.﴾ [Maryam: 54–55].

﴿And mention in the Book Ismail﴾ — he is the son of Ibrahim, peace be upon them both. He singled out his mention apart from the mention of his father and his brother, to show the utmost care for his matter, by presenting him independently. His saying, ﴿Indeed, he was true to his promise﴾, is a justification for the command. Mentioning him, peace be upon him, with this attribute, although the rest of the prophets share it with him, is an honouring and a dignifying of him. And because it is the best-known of his qualities. And consider that he promised himself to endure patience at being sacrificed, and he fulfilled it when he said: ﴿You will find me, if Allah wills, among the patient﴾, and this is the greatest that can be imagined in that regard. In it is also an alert to the great worth of this trait; for this reason its opposite is hypocrisy, as the reports have stated explicitly. ﴿And he was a messenger and a prophet.﴾ ﴿And he used to enjoin on his family prayer and zakah﴾ [Maryam: 55], i.e., he would begin with his family in commanding righteousness and worship, so as to make them an example for those after them. And because they have the first claim over the rest of people: ﴿And warn your closest kindred﴾ [al-Shu'ara': 214]; ﴿And enjoin prayer upon your family﴾ [Ta-Ha: 132]; ﴿Save yourselves and your families from a Fire﴾ [al-Tahrim: 6]. This was conveyed by al-Zamakhshari. ﴿And he was pleasing to his Lord﴾ [Maryam: 55], i.e., due to his being characterised by the sublime qualities of which those mentioned are among them.

Commentary of al-Qasimi (Mahasin al-Ta'wil) on surah 19, verses 56–57:

The discussion of the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

[56] ﴿And mention in the Book Idris. Indeed, he was a man of truth and a prophet.﴾ [57] ﴿And We raised him to a high station.﴾ [Maryam: 57].

﴿And mention in the Book Idris. Indeed, he was a man of truth and a prophet.﴾ ﴿And We raised him to a high station.﴾ [Maryam: 57] refers to the nobility of prophethood and nearness to Allah, exalted is He. So the elevation is figurative (ma'nawi). Or He raised him bodily, alive, to the heaven. Al-Shihab said: It has been said: the second is closer, because an elevation associated with a place cannot be figurative. But this is open to question, for the like of it occurs, and even something more evident than it, such as his saying:

"Be in a place where, if you fall, you stand up, while your two feet are in good health."

End of quote. What supports the second view is what is related in the two Sahih collections (Sahihayn) from Anas, in the hadith of the Mi'raj (Night Journey and Ascension), that he, may the blessings of Allah be upon him, saw Idris in the fourth heaven. Idris is Ilyas (Elijah), whose mention comes in Surat al-Saffat, and he is called Elijah (Ilya) in the Torah. Regarding his being raised to heaven there is a wondrous report, and perhaps the noble revelation in this verse alluded to it, and Allah knows best.

(p-٤١٥٢) The discussion on the interpretation of His words, exalted is He:

[58] ﴿Those are the ones upon whom Allah bestowed favor from among the prophets, of the descendants of Adam, and of those We carried with Noah, and of the descendants of Abraham and Israel, and of those whom We guided and chose. When the verses of the Most Merciful were recited to them, they fell down prostrating and weeping.﴾

﴿Those﴾ refers to those mentioned in the surah, from Zakariyya up to Idris, peace be upon him. The word "those" with the sense of distance indicates the elevated status of these people and the great distance of their rank in virtue. His words, exalted is He, ﴿upon whom Allah bestowed favor﴾, mean: with the various kinds of religious and worldly blessings. ﴿from among the prophets, of the descendants of Adam, and of those We carried with Noah, and of the descendants of Abraham and Israel, and of those whom We guided and chose﴾, meaning: We guided them to the truth and chose them for prophethood and honor. ﴿When the verses of the Most Merciful were recited to them, they fell down prostrating and weeping﴾, meaning: when they heard the speech of Allah containing His proofs, evidences and demonstrations, they prostrated to their Lord in humility and submission, despite their elevated rank and their high nearness to Him, exalted is He. In the verse there is a recommendation of prostration and weeping upon hearing the recitation.

Ibn Kathir said: The scholars have agreed on the legitimacy of prostration here, following them and emulating their way. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated that Umar ibn al-Khattab, may Allah be pleased with him, recited Surat Maryam and prostrated, and he said: "This is the prostration, so where is the weeping?"

Commentary of al-Qasimi (Mahasin al-Ta'wil) on surah 19, verse 59:

When the Exalted mentioned the party of the blessed, who are the prophets and those who followed them among those who uphold the limits and commands of God, He mentioned those who cast aside their call from among those who came after them, and what will befall them, by His words, glorified is He:

The discussion on the interpretation of His words, exalted is He:

[59] ﴿Then there succeeded them a generation who neglected the prayer and followed their desires, so they will encounter error﴾.

﴿Then there succeeded them a generation who neglected the prayer﴾. It is also read (al-Salawat), in the plural, meaning: those which include prostrations and remembrances, which invite weeping. And if they neglect them, then they are even more neglectful of what is other than them of the obligations, because it is the pillar of the religion, its foundation, and the best of the deeds of the servants. ﴿And followed their desires﴾, meaning: they committed what contradicts weeping and the matters that please God of good conduct and deeds, through immersion in acts of disobedience which are the forerunner of disbelief. ﴿So they will encounter error (ghayy)﴾, meaning: evil. Al-Zamakhshari said: every evil is ghayy among the Arabs, and every good is rushad (right guidance). Al-Muraqqish said:

*Whoever encounters good, people will praise his affair, and whoever goes astray will not lack blame for his error.*

That is, whoever does good, people will praise his affair; and whoever does evil will not lack reproaches for his action. It was also said: the poet meant by "good" wealth, and by "ghayy" poverty, that is: whoever becomes poor. And from it is the one who said:

*Among people, whoever encounters good, they speak to him of what he desires, and the mother of the one who errs is bereaved.*

That is, the bereavement (al-thakl). It is also permissible that the meaning be the recompense of ghayy, like His words: ﴿He will encounter a penalty (athaman)﴾ [al-Furqan: 68], meaning: evil and punishment. So it is applied to it as ghayy is applied to its consequent recompense, metaphorically; or: ghayy means deviation from the path of Paradise. Thus it has its well-known meaning.

Commentary of al-Qasimi (Mahasin al-Ta'wil) on surah 19, verses 60–61:

(p-4154) The discussion on the interpretation of His saying, Exalted is He:

[60] ﴿Except for those who repent, believe, and do righteous deeds; for those will enter Paradise and will not be wronged in the least.﴾ [61] ﴿Gardens of perpetual residence, which the Most Merciful has promised His servants in the unseen. Indeed, His promise is ever fulfilled.﴾ [Maryam: 61].

﴿Except for those who repent﴾, i.e., from neglecting the prayers and following desires. ﴿And believe and do righteous deeds; for those will enter Paradise and will not be wronged in the least.﴾ ﴿Gardens of perpetual residence, which the Most Merciful has promised His servants in the unseen﴾ [Maryam: 61]. The phrase "in the unseen" is connected to a hidden pronoun referring back to the Gardens. Or, it refers to His servants, meaning: He promised them the Gardens while they are associated with the unseen, i.e., the Gardens are absent from them and not present, or they are absent from the Gardens and do not see them, and they believed in them only by means of report. Or, it is connected to a hidden element that is the cause of the promise, meaning: He promised them the Gardens because of their faith. This was stated by Abu al-Su'ud. ﴿Indeed, His promise is ever fulfilled﴾ [Maryam: 61], i.e., He does not break it.

**On the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:**

[62] ﴿They will not hear therein any vain speech, only "Peace." And they will have their provision therein morning and evening.﴾ [63] ﴿That is the Garden which We cause to inherit from among Our servants those who were God-fearing.﴾ [Maryam: 63].

﴿They will not hear therein any vain speech, only "Peace"﴾ means: they will not hear therein any superfluous speech that is of no benefit. This is a *kinaya* (metonymy, an indirect expression) for the absence of vain speech coming from its people. Al-Zamakhshari, may Allah have mercy on him, said: "This contains a clear reminder of the obligation to avoid vain speech and guard against it, since Allah has declared the Abode free of it, the Abode in which there is no obligation." How excellent is His, glory be to Him, saying: ﴿When they pass by vain talk, they pass by with dignity﴾ [al-Furqan: 72], and ﴿When they hear vain talk, they turn away from it and say: "To us our deeds and to you your deeds. Peace be upon you. We do not seek the ignorant."﴾ [al-Qasas: 55]. We seek refuge with Allah from vain talk, ignorance, and plunging into what does not concern us.

(p. 4155) The meaning of ﴿only "Peace"﴾ is: a greeting of peace (*taslim*), namely the greeting of the angels to them, or of some of them to others. This is an *istithna' munqati'* (disconnected exception), as He said: ﴿They will not hear therein any vain speech or sinful talk﴾ [al-Waqi'ah: 25], ﴿only the saying "Peace, peace"﴾ [al-Waqi'ah: 26]. ﴿And they will have their provision therein morning and evening﴾, ﴿That is the Garden which We cause to inherit from among Our servants those who were God-fearing﴾ [Maryam: 63]. They are those characterized by the branches of faith (*shu'ab al-iman*), which are enumerated in various places in the verses of the Qur'an.

When He, glory be to Him, related the accounts of the prophets, peace be upon them, what He related, affirming it, and followed it with what the later generations had innovated, and mentioned their reward, He followed that with the narration of the descent of Jibril, peace be upon him. This was a refutation of what the polytheists claimed, that he [the Prophet] had been forsaken and that [Jibril] did not visit him. It was a consolation for him (ﷺ) and an informing that the situation is not as those later generations claimed. So He, glory be to Him, said:
