The discussion on the interpretation of His, the Exalted, saying:

﴿We do not descend except by the command of your Lord. To Him belongs what is before us, what is behind us, and what is between that. And your Lord is never forgetful.﴾

That is: He does not forget anything at all. Rather, He does not pour forth knowledge or send down an angel except for a wisdom for which the situation is prepared. That is: the non-descent is only due to the absence of a command for it, and it was not because of His leaving you or abandoning you. In the repetition of the name "your Lord," which indicates the bringing of the matter to its fitting perfection and is attributed to his pronoun (peace be upon him), there is an honouring of him and an indication of the reason for the ruling, which is not hidden.

And His, the Exalted, saying:

Commentary of al-Qasimi (Mahasin al-Ta'wil) on surah 19, verse 65:

The discussion of the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

[65] ﴿Lord of the heavens and the earth and whatever is between them. So worship Him and be steadfast in His worship. Do you know of any who is worthy of His name?﴾

﴿Lord of the heavens and the earth and whatever is between them﴾ That is: of the planets, the stars, the clouds and other things. (p-4156) Some of the astronomers ('ulama' al-falak) said: the verse indicates that the heavens are more than seven, and that the mention of seven is not for restriction, as we have stated in Surat al-Baqara, that by "the heavens" are meant the celestial bodies, and the earth is one of them. Abu al-Su'ud said: the verse is an explanation of the impossibility of forgetfulness on His part, for how can it be conceived that heedlessness and forgetfulness should approach the court of His glory, when the dominion of the heavens and the earth and whatever is between them is in His hand? It is a omitted predicate, or it is a substitute for "your Lord." ﴿So worship Him and be steadfast in His worship﴾ That is: persist in it constantly. His saying ﴿Do you know of any who is worthy of His name?﴾ That is: a like or an equal, so that you may turn to Him and direct your face toward Him, and what you seek will be poured out upon you. The sentence is an affirmation of the obligation of worshipping Him alone. That is: once it is established that there is none like Him, and that none other than Him deserves worship, there is no alternative to submitting to His command and carrying out His worship, and enduring its hardships.

The interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

[66] ﴿And man says, "When I have died, will I really be brought forth alive?"﴾

﴿And man says, "When I have died, will I really be brought forth alive?"﴾ That is: he says, by way of denial and disbelief: "Will I be brought out after I have remained in the grave for a period?"

The discussion of His saying, exalted is He:

[67] ﴿Does not man remember that We created him before, when he was nothing?﴾

﴿Does not man remember that We created him before, when he was nothing?﴾ That is: before We made him dust and a drop of semen. He was pure non-existence, with no being in concrete reality. So restoring him is not far-fetched.

Abu al-Su'ud said: The use of the explicit noun ("man") in place of the pronoun adds emphasis to the affirmation that humanity is a motive for reflecting upon the states of creation that befell him, which are meant to turn him away from the aforementioned statement. This is the reason it is attributed to the species, or to the individual under that designation. That is: how strange is man in his denial and his failure to remember what was mentioned, when it is He who gave him the intellect to reflect upon outcomes, and who bestowed upon him the creation of the heavens and the earth and what lies between them, so that he might know the Benefactor, thank Him, and worship Him, and so be recompensed for his deed.

**The discussion on the interpretation of His saying, may He be exalted:**

[68] ﴿So by your Lord, We will surely gather them and the devils; then We will surely bring them around Hell on their knees.﴾

﴿So by your Lord, We will surely gather them and the devils﴾: that is, We will surely gather those who denied the resurrection together with the devils who misled them and led them astray from the truth. ﴿Then We will surely bring them around Hell on their knees﴾: *جِثِيًّا* is the plural of *جاثٍ* (kneeling), from *جَثا*, meaning one who sits upon his knees. This is because of the terror of the *maṭla'* (the place of arrival, i.e., the moment of entering the scene of judgment). So they will not be able to stand, as in His saying, ﴿And you will see every nation kneeling﴾ [al-Jathiyah: 28].

Commentary of al-Qasimi (Mahasin al-Ta'wil) on surah 19, verse 69:

The discussion of the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

[69] ﴿Then We will surely drag out from every sect those of them who were most insolent against the Most Merciful.﴾

﴿Then We will surely drag out from every sect those of them who were most insolent against the Most Merciful.﴾ That is: We will certainly bring out to the Fire, from every group, the one who is most insolent toward the Most Merciful, the One who showed mercy to them by sending down the Book, sending the Messenger, and making known the harms of desires through reason and transmitted texts. ﴿Insolence (ʿitiyyan)﴾ means audacity, by preferring desires over His command and by not caring about Him.

Commentary of al-Qasimi (Mahasin al-Ta'wil) on surah 19, verse 70:

The discussion of the interpretation of His words, exalted is He:

[70] ﴿Then indeed We are most knowing of those who most deserve to burn therein.﴾

﴿Then indeed We are most knowing of those who most deserve to burn therein.﴾ They are the ones who pull away (al-muntaza'un). Indeed they are the most deserving of the factions (ash-shiya'), since they went astray for the sake of the pleasures of this world and its desires. Thus they became the most deserving of burning therein, and so they are singled out for a doubled punishment.

The discussion of the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

[71] ﴿And there is none of you but will pass over it. That is ever, with your Lord, a decreed matter that must be carried out.﴾

﴿And there is none of you but will pass over it﴾, i.e., none of you, whether righteous or wicked, but he will come to it (wāridūhā, "passing over it"). ﴿That is ever, with your Lord, a decreed matter that must be carried out﴾, i.e., a judgment that is firm, definite, and settled.

(p-4158) The discussion of the interpretation of His saying, Exalted is He:

[72] ﴿Then We shall deliver those who were mindful of God, and We shall leave the wrongdoers therein, kneeling.﴾

﴿Then﴾ means: after the arrival and the bringing forth, for clarification. ﴿We shall deliver those who were mindful of God, and We shall leave the wrongdoers therein, kneeling﴾ means: they will be unable to pass beyond it (i.e., Hell).

Al-Zamakhshari said: In it is evidence that what is meant by "arrival" (wurud) is kneeling around it (jithiy), and that the believers separate from the disbelievers toward Paradise after their kneeling, while the disbelievers remain in their places, kneeling.

The Discussion on the Interpretation of His, the Exalted, Statement:

[73] ﴿When Our clear verses are recited to them, those who disbelieve say to those who believe, "Which of the two groups is better in station and finer in assembly?"﴾.

﴿When Our clear verses are recited to them, those who disbelieve say to those who believe, "Which of the two groups is better in station"﴾ means: in place and position. ﴿And finer in assembly﴾ means: in gathering of people. The meaning is that when the verses of God, the Exalted, with clear proof and evident demonstration of their purposes, are recited to these disbelievers, they turn away and begin to argue for the superiority of their own state by reason of their greater share of this world, since they have finer dwellings, loftier homes, more populous gatherings, and more frequent visitors and comers. In other words: how could we be upon falsehood when we are in this position, while those who hide in the house of al-Arqam ibn Abi al-Arqam are upon the truth? As God, the Exalted, said, reporting about them: ﴿And those who disbelieve say to those who believe, "Had it been good, they would not have preceded us to it"﴾ [al-Ahqaf: 11]. And the people of Noah said: ﴿"Shall we believe you when the lowest of people follow you?"﴾ [al-Shu'ara': 111]. And He, the Exalted, said: ﴿And thus We tested some of them by means of others, so that they would say, "Are these the ones upon whom God has bestowed favor from among us?" Is God not most knowing of the grateful?﴾ [al-An'am: 53].

And thus He refuted their doubt with His, the Glorified, statement:

(p-4159) The explanation of His saying, exalted is He:

[74] ﴿How many generations We destroyed before them, who were better in furnishings and appearance.﴾

﴿How many generations We destroyed before them, who were better in furnishings⦆ — meaning, in property (matā'an). ﴿And appearance⦆ — meaning, in sight and bearing, from the greatness of their standing. Yet it did not avail them anything against the punishment of God. As He, exalted is He, said about the people of Pharaoh, who were drowned: ﴿How much they left behind of gardens and springs﴾ [al-Dukhan: 25] ﴿and crops and a noble station﴾ [al-Dukhan: 26]. As for ﴿ri'yan⦆, it is a verbal noun used in the sense of a passive participle (fi'l bi-ma'na maf'ul), like al-ṭiḥn (الطِّحْن), meaning "that which is ground."

The Interpretation of His Words, Exalted is He:

[75] ﴿Say: "Whoever is in error, let the Most Merciful extend [his term] for him in extension, until, when they see what they are promised, either the punishment or the Hour, they will know who is worse in position and weaker in soldiers."﴾

﴿Say: "Whoever is in error, let the Most Merciful extend [his term] for him in extension"﴾ That is: whoever is immersed in ignorance and heedlessness of the outcomes of affairs, and they are those mentioned before, and whoever resembles them. ﴿Let the Most Merciful extend [his term] for him﴾ That is: He extends for him and gives him respite by lengthening his life and granting him wealth. Its being expressed in the form of a command is to signify that this is something that ought to be done in accordance with the requirements of wisdom, in order to cut off excuses, as His saying, Exalted is He, indicates: ﴿Did We not give you a life long enough that whoever would be mindful might be mindful therein?﴾ [Fatir: 37]. Or it is for istidraj (gradual enticement), as His saying, Exalted is He, reveals: ﴿We only give them respite so that they may increase in sin﴾ [Al 'Imran: 178]. It has also been said that what is meant by it is a supplication for extension, respite and delay. That is: may Allah grant him respite in what he is in, until he meets his Lord and his term comes to an end, either by a punishment that befalls him, or the Hour suddenly. Almighty Allah has specified the limit of the extension by His saying: ﴿until, when they see what they are promised, either the punishment or the Hour, they will know who is worse in position and weaker in soldiers﴾ That is: in party and helpers.

(p-4160) The discussion on the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

[77] ﴿Have you seen the one who disbelieved in Our verses and said, "I will surely be given wealth and children"?﴾

﴿Have you seen the one who disbelieved in Our verses and said, "I will surely be given"﴾, i.e., in the Hereafter, ﴿wealth and children﴾, meaning: look at this speaker who dares to pronounce on the unseen, how disbelieving he is.

The discussion concerning the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

[78] ﴿Has he looked into the Unseen, or has he taken a covenant with the Most Merciful?﴾

﴿Has he looked into the Unseen, or has he taken a covenant with the Most Merciful?﴾ That is: (he has obtained knowledge) by this, because knowledge of it cannot be reached except by one of these two ways.

[79] ﴿Nay! We shall record what he says and extend for him an extension of punishment.﴾ [80] ﴿And We will inherit from him what he says, and he will come to Us alone.﴾ [Maryam: 80]

﴿Nay! We shall record what he says﴾, i.e., We shall preserve it against him, to hold him accountable for it. ﴿And extend for him an extension of punishment﴾ by multiplying it for him, as recompense for his mockery.

﴿And We will inherit from him what he says﴾ [Maryam: 80], i.e., We will strip from him the wealth and children that We had granted him, (p-4161) so that neither remains with him, such that it could avert the punishment from him. ﴿And he will come to Us alone﴾ [Maryam: 80], i.e., on the Day of Gathering, with neither wealth nor child accompanying him. Al-Bukhari narrated from Khabbab, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: "I was a qayn (blacksmith) in the Jahiliyyah in Makkah. Commentary of al-Qasimi (Mahasin al-Ta'wil) on surah 19, verse 82:

The discussion of the interpretation of His words, exalted is He:

[82] ﴿Nay! They will deny their worship of them, and they will be opponents to them.﴾

﴿Nay!﴾ That is: the matter is not as they assumed, and what they hoped for will not happen. ﴿They will deny their worship of them﴾ That is: the gods will disavow their deserving of worship. ﴿And they will be opponents to them﴾ That is: they will wish their destruction, when they bring them into the ruin of the claim of partnership (shirk), as He, exalted is He, said: ﴿And who is more astray than one who calls upon other than Allah, one who will not respond to him until the Day of Resurrection, and they are unaware of their supplication?﴾ [al-Ahqaf: 5] ﴿And when the people are gathered, they will be enemies to them and will deny their worship﴾ [al-Ahqaf: 6]. But they will throw the word at them: "Indeed, you are liars."﴾ [al-Nahl: 86]

It has been said: what is meant by the gods is those among rational beings who were worshipped, because of the application of the pronoun for rational beings to them and their speech. And it has been said: the idols, with Allah creating in them the power of speech, so that what is applied to rational beings is applied to them. And it has been said: the more general of the two, which is the more apparent.

The Interpretation of His Words, Exalted is He:

[83] ﴿Have you not seen that We have sent the devils upon the disbelievers, inciting them with [strong] incitement?﴾

﴿Have you not seen that We have sent the devils upon the disbelievers?﴾ That is: by empowering them over them and enabling them to lead them astray. Or: We have appointed them for them, so that they prevail over them. ﴿Inciting them with [strong] incitement﴾ means: they stir them up and agitate them toward sins, through embellishments and making desires seem appealing, with intense agitation.

Al-Zamakhshari said: al-azz (incitement), al-hazz (shaking), and al-istifzaz (provocation) are siblings. Their meaning is stirring up and intense agitation. The purpose [of this verse] is to astonish the Messenger of God (ﷺ), after the verses in which the insolent and rebellious among the disbelievers were mentioned, along with their sayings, their scheming, their obstinacy toward the messengers, their mockery, and their gathering to reject the truth after its clarity and the absence of doubt about it, and their immersion in that through following the devils and what they adorn for them. Thus this verse serves as a concluding appendage (tadhyil) to what precedes it. And His words, Exalted is He:

On the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

[84] ﴿So do not be hasty against them; We are only counting out for them a counted number.﴾

﴿So do not be hasty against them﴾, i.e., in bringing the punishment upon them, so that He may purify the earth of them. The (fa') here indicates that what precedes it is a likely cause for the forbidden act to occur, which necessitates the prohibition. One says: "عَجَّلْتَ عَلَيْهِ بِكَذا" (ʿajjalta ʿalayhi bi-kadhā) when you ask him to hasten it from him. His saying, exalted is He, ﴿We are only counting out for them a counted number﴾, is an explanation of the reason for the prohibition, by showing that their destruction is near. That is: We only defer them to a specified, fixed term. A similar statement is His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And do not seek to hasten [the punishment] for them. On the day they see what they are promised, it will be as if they had not remained but an hour of a day﴾ [al-Ahqaf: 35].

(p-4163) Al-Shihab said: Counting ('add) is a metaphor for scarcity, and its scarcity is due to its coming to an end and its perishing, as al-Ma'mun said: "Whatever has a number, and has no extension, how swiftly it is exhausted." This does not contradict what passed, that He prolongs [the term] for one who is in error; that is, He lengthens it, because it is relative to the apparent state of affairs in their view. It is few in terms of its outcome and in the sight of God. How excellent is the saying of the poet:

"Indeed the beloved among the loved ones is snatched away; no doorkeeper or guard prevents death."

"And how can a youth rejoice in this world and its pleasures, when his utterance and his breaths are counted against him?"

The discussion of the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

[85] ﴿On the Day We shall gather the God-fearing to the Most Merciful as a delegation﴾.

﴿On the Day We shall gather the God-fearing to the Most Merciful as a delegation﴾: i.e., coming to Him as visitors (wafidin). The essence of wufud (delegation) is arriving before the great ones for gifts and for seeking their bounty. Therein is an indication of honouring and magnifying them, both the one visited and the one who visits.

The discussion of the words of the Exalted:

[86] ﴿And We will drive the criminals to Hell in thirst.﴾

﴿And We will drive the criminals to Hell in thirst.﴾ That is: thirsty. Mentioning their being driven (بِالسُّوقِ, al-suq) indicates their humiliation and debasement, as if they were thirsty cattle being driven to water. Al-warid (الوِرْدُ) is the going to water, and it is also applied to those who go to it. And the words of the Exalted:

The discussion of the words of His saying, may He be exalted:

[87] ﴿They will not have power of intercession, except one who has taken a covenant with the Most Merciful.﴾

﴿They will not have power of intercession, except one who has taken a covenant with the Most Merciful.﴾ The pronoun refers to their idols, mentioned earlier in His saying: ﴿And they have taken gods besides Allah﴾ [Maryam: 81]. It is a rebuttal of their worshippers in their claim (p-4164) that the idols are their intercessors with Allah. Taking a covenant (ʿahd) means faith and righteous deeds. That is: rather, whoever believes and does righteous deeds, he will intercede for the sinners, according to what Allah the Exalted has promised. It is also permissible for the covenant to mean permission and command. It is said: "I took permission (idhn) to do such-and-such, and I took it (ittakhadhtuhu) with the same meaning," from the usage of "the commander covenanted (ʿahida) with so-and-so to do such-and-such," if he commanded him to do it. That is: none intercedes except one who is commanded to intercede and given permission for it. This is supported by passages in the Revelation: ﴿And how many an angel in the heavens whose intercession avails nothing except after Allah permits for whom He wills and approves﴾ [al-Najm: 26]; ﴿And intercession does not benefit with Him except for one whom He has permitted﴾ [Saba: 23]; ﴿On that Day, intercession will not benefit except one whom the Most Merciful has permitted and whose word He approves﴾ [Ta-Ha: 109]. Similar to this verse is His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And those they invoke besides Him do not have power of intercession, except one who testifies to the truth while they know﴾ [al-Zukhruf: 86].

Commentary of al-Qasimi (Mahasin al-Ta'wil) on surah 19, verse 96:

After detailing the evil ways of the disbelievers, He, glory be to Him, followed it with the good qualities of the righteous, so He said:

The discussion concerning the interpretation (ta'wil) of His saying, exalted is He:

[96] ﴿Indeed, those who have believed and done righteous deeds, the Most Merciful will bring about for them affection.﴾

﴿Indeed, those who have believed and done righteous deeds, the Most Merciful will bring about for them affection.﴾ That is: He will plant love and affection for them in the hearts of His righteous servants, without any reliance upon the means that earn affection. This is what they said in its interpretation. Abu Muslim said: its meaning is that He will bestow upon them what they love. He said: "Wadd (affection) and mahabbah (love) are the same. One says: 'I gave so-and-so his love (ataytu fulanan mahabbatahu),' and 'He gave them what they love, and I gave him his wadd.'" And among their expressions: "I wadadtu (I wished/loved) that it were so-and-so," meaning: I loved. So its meaning is: "The Most Merciful will give them their wadd," i.e., what they love in Paradise. Then Abu Muslim said: "This second view is preferable for several reasons:

The first: How can the first view be valid, given our knowledge that the pious Muslim is hated by the disbelievers, and many Muslims also hate him?

The second: Such love may occur more for disbelievers and sinners, so how can it be taken as a favor toward the believers?

The third: Their love in the hearts is by their own doing. Therefore, interpreting the verse as the granting of otherworldly benefits is preferable." End of quotation. Al-Razi attempted to obscure the choice of the first view and the answer to the second. But the truth is more deserving of being followed. And His saying, exalted is He:

**The interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:**

[97] ﴿So We have made it easy only in your tongue, that you may give glad tidings thereby to the God-conscious and warn thereby a people contentious.﴾

﴿So We have made it easy only in your tongue﴾, that is: We made this Qur'an easy by means of your language. ﴿That you may give glad tidings thereby to the God-conscious﴾, that is, to those who guard themselves against the punishment of God by performing His obligations and avoiding His prohibitions, with Paradise. ﴿And warn thereby a people contentious﴾, that is, you warn your people of the Quraysh of God's punishment through this Qur'an. For they are people of *luddin* (contentiousness) and disputation in falsehood, who do not accept the truth. *Luddun* is the intensity of hostility. The *ba'* (the preposition "in") in His saying ﴿in your tongue﴾ carries the sense of *'ala* (upon), meaning: upon your language. Or the verb *taysir* (making easy) is taken to include the sense of *inzal* (sending down), meaning: We made the Qur'an easy, sending it down in your language, so that its conveyance, understanding and memorization would be facilitated.

Al-Zamakhshari said: This is the conclusion and close of the surah. It is as if He said: Convey this revealed text, or give glad tidings with it and warn with it, for We have sent it down, etc. That is, the *fa'* (the particle "so/therefore") here gives the reason for a command toward which the noble composition (*al-nazm al-karim*) leads.

(p-4167) Al-Razi said: By this, He pointed out the great standing of this surah, because of what it contains of divine unity, prophethood, resurrection and gathering, and the refutation of the sects of misguiders and falsifiers. And that He made that easy for the glad tidings to the God-conscious and the warning to those who oppose them. He reminded them with the most eloquent description of a thing, which is *luddun*, because the *alad* (the one most contentious) is the one who clings to falsehood and argues about it.

Then, exalted is He, concluded this surah with an eloquent admonition, and so He said, exalted is He:

Commentary of al-Qasimi (Mahasin al-Ta'wil) on surah 19, verse 98:

The discussion of His saying, exalted is He:

[98] ﴿And how many generations have We destroyed before them? Do you perceive any one of them, or hear from them a faint sound?﴾

﴿And how many generations have We destroyed before them﴾, that is, peoples of strife (qawm Ludd), like these, with a great destruction: ﴿Do you perceive any one of them﴾, that is, sense him and see him: ﴿or hear from them a faint sound﴾, that is, a hidden sound.

The meaning is that they perished and were destroyed, their homes were emptied of them, and their dwellings became desolate of them. Likewise, these people are heading toward what those came to, unless they make amends through repentance.
